title: Many reports do not mean many incidents
source_notes: Redrawn schematic: repeated reports, nearby distinct incidents and a false-only report cluster. No actual report locations or field imagery. Paper 6444, Introduction / RQ1 / RQ3.

title: Related approaches and the study gap
source_notes: [1] Blondel et al. (2008); [5] Gralla et al. (2014); [6] Sakaki et al. (2010); [7] CrisisMMD; [8] FloodNet.

title: Research questions: do safeguards improve dispatch?
source_notes: paper/main.tex:150–168, 486–543; RQs moved ahead of technical definitions.

title: Observable pipeline: reports to a fixed schedule
source_notes: Paper 6444, Figure 1 / Algorithms 1–2. Schematic observable-only inference and frozen-output evaluation. Missingness path is specified but not an empirically validated RQ1 result.

title: Generator 3.0: what does one run contain?
source_notes: paper/main.tex:441–454; thucnghiem/data/README.md; gold/run_001/run_manifest.json. [9–11]. Icons are schematic, not report images.

title: Why two generators? Different questions need different truth
source_notes: paper/main.tex:441–469, 486–543. Candidate 4.1: 339–424 reports/dataset. Its outcomes are not inferred from the priority formula.

title: Why test Product? Geography gates the whole affinity
source_notes: paper/main.tex:250–325; [2] spatial–range product precedent. Pair values are invented teaching inputs, not benchmark results or tuned parameters. Retention thresholds and actual pipeline settings are not compared by this example.

title: Louvain: local moves and graph aggregation
source_notes: Original editable schematic of Louvain local movement and graph aggregation; Blondel et al. (2008). Node positions and colors are pedagogical, not measured rescue data. Self-loops represent aggregate internal weights; detection approximates modularity optimization.

title: Bounded priority limits copies, not dishonest claims
source_notes: paper/main.tex:380–421, 620–677. The confidence Q is a heuristic, not a calibrated probability of truth. Fixed-family exact copies differ from changed or coordinated payloads.

title: Evaluation protocol and information boundaries
source_notes: Paper 6444, Experimental Design. RQ1 fixed stresses receive no retuning; RQ3 primary inference uses 40 seed-level pairs.

title: One held-out run: compare groups with withheld truth
source_notes: [3] Hubert & Arabie (1985); paper/main.tex:522–543. Six-dot partitions are schematic and have no displayed measured ARI. ARI is not percent correctly classified. Independent units are runs, not individual report pairs.

title: Reported metrics: ranking and score stability
source_notes: [4] Järvelin & Kekäläinen (2002); RQ2 notebook uses sklearn.ndcg_score with linear benefit gains. Spearman / overlap are secondary.

title: Reported metrics: dispatch outcomes
source_notes: Paper 6444, RQ3; RQ3_EndToEnd_Dispatch_Colab.ipynb, outcomes and metrics. Other operational endpoints remain complementary.

title: RQ1: no Product composition advantage is established
source_notes: paper/main.tex:548–591; benchmark_summary.csv. 16.49% is the fraction of predicted destinations that are false, not the fraction of fake reports. Zero fake absorption does not imply fake rejection. CIs are unadjusted bootstrap intervals.

title: RQ1: fivefold copies expose a major failure case
source_notes: paper/main.tex:593–618; rq1_stress_paired_effects.csv. Displayed interval is the unadjusted paired-bootstrap 95% CI. MD = matched-density. Zero change for DBSCAN does not mean high absolute accuracy; two copy levels do not identify a collapse threshold.

title: RQ2: exact-copy stability has a narrow scope
source_notes: Paper 6444, Table 3 / §4.2; exported RQ2 robustness summaries. Revised campaign drift .1688; legacy .0309.

title: RQ2: alignment with simulated benefit remains weak
source_notes: Paper 6444, §4.2; exported RQ2 alignment summaries. Intervals: bootstrap 95%; linear independent-benefit gains.

title: RQ3: safeguards do not ensure better dispatch
source_notes: Paper 6444, Figure 3 / §4.3; descriptive condition means. Primary tests average conditions within seed, retaining 40 pairs.

title: Three contributions, with explicit evidence limits
source_notes: paper/main.tex:150–188, 250–325, 380–421, 756–800. Three contributions are conditional theory, invariant scoring and a staged downstream audit; simulated evidence does not validate source authenticity or field policy.

title: Conclusion: stage safeguards do not establish dispatch benefit
source_notes: paper/main.tex:756–800. Proved properties, within-generator results and deployment claims remain separate evidence layers.

title: Future work: close the evidence gaps
source_notes: Author-facing proposals derived from Paper 6444, Discussion and Threats to Validity; not completed field validation.
